answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: an agent must complete verifiable jobs before its reputation carries payout weight, like a plume of credentials that grows only through real task completion. Each new identity starts worthless, so attackers registering thousands of fake walnuts must perform all that labor before earning anything. Wandering between cheap identities for fresh payouts is therefore unprofitable: mass-registration costs more in verified work than any payout could return.
